title: client-priority-preemptive-cancel-and-orphaned-stream-reclamation
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Customers run mixed-priority workloads on the same serving pools. Long-running streams from low-priority clients can tie up GPU concurrency and KV cache slots, causing high-priority, latency-sensitive clients to miss SLOs when they cancel or disconnect mid-stream. This PR adds a server-side preemptive cancel mechanism combined with an orphaned-stream reclamation flow so that: (1) clients can mark a request as high-priority and preempt lower-priority in-flight streams; (2) when a client cancels or disconnects without a clean teardown, the server reclaims resources deterministically after a short quarantine window; (3) in-flight function/tool calls are tombstoned or re-associated with idempotency tokens to avoid double-execution. Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes; new optional headers are introduced (X-Stream-Priority, X-Preempt-Token) and resume semantics are extended. The description below covers design, implementation, tests, and rollout notes.
commits: 3 commits: 1) runtime: add StreamPriority enum and scheduler preemption hooks; 2) sessionmgr: implement preempt token handshake, quarantine timer, tombstone flow; 3) api: add header parsing, docs and tests. High-level commit messages included; unit tests and lightweight e2e harness added.
discussion: Arjun Patel (reviewer): Can you explain how preempt tokens are generated and what entropy guarantees we need? Also how does this interact with private deployments where a governance VPC restricts random source entropy?

Maya Chen (author): Preempt tokens are 72-bit cryptographically generated nonces produced by the session owner when acquiring a preempt window. They are short-lived (default 30s) and rotated on resume. For private installs we fall back to the node's CSPRNG; we added documentation in docs/api/streams.md and a config knob for enabling external KMS-backed RNG (see sessionmgr.PreemptConfig).
Lucia Gomez (reviewer): We need clearer metrics to track reclaimed streams vs preempted cancels. Add histograms and counters so SRE can alert on abnormal reclamation rates.
Maya Chen (author): Added metrics: stream_reclaims_total, stream_preempts_total, stream_tombstones_total and a reclaim_latency_seconds histogram. Also wired tags for customer_id and priority.
Samir Rao (reviewer): How do function/tool calls behave if they were mid-execution when a stream was tombstoned? Risk of at-least-once semantics causing duplicate side-effects.

Maya Chen (author): For in-flight tool calls we added an explicit tombstone marker that includes the original idempotency token, request checksum and tool-call state. Workers will honor tombstones: if a tool worker observes a tombstoned call it will either noop (if it can detect idempotent duplicate) or return a ControlledTombstoneError which the runtime maps to an application-level CANCELLED event. We documented the migration guidance for integrators in the API doc.
Arjun Patel (reviewer): Request small change: extend telemetry labels to include head_branch and runtime_version for postmortem correlation.
Maya Chen (author): Added labels and updated metrics YAML. Tests updated accordingly.
release_notes: Add optional client priority header and server-side preemptive cancel to reclaim compute from low-priority orphaned streams. New headers: X-Stream-Priority (low|normal|high), X-Preempt-Token for controlled preemption. Metrics: stream_reclaims_total, stream_preempts_total, stream_tombstones_total. No breaking changes; recommended to opt-in in early rollout.
notes_for_ops: Rollout plan: gated feature flag 'preemptive_reclaim_v1' enabled for 10% of traffic for 48h, monitor stream_reclaims_total and reclaim_latency_seconds. If reclamation rate spikes > 3x baseline roll back feature flag. Private installer: add sessionmgr.PreemptConfig to values.yaml; default disabled on on-prem clusters to avoid entropy/KMS assumptions.
qa_summary: Unit tests: scheduler preemption and tombstone state transitions covered. E2E: lightweight harness simulates high-priority client preempting low-priority long-running streaming request; verified GPU slot reclaim and client-visible CANCELLED event. CI flake: initial e2e intermittently failed due to timing in test harness; rerun succeeded.
docs_updated: docs/api/streams.md, sdk/python example, release notes entry
migration_steps: No forced migration. Clients wanting preemption must set X-Stream-Priority and optionally call /v1/streams/preempt with a generated preempt token. Operators: enable feature flag and optionally configure PreemptConfig.reclaim_window_seconds (default 12) and preempt_window_seconds (default 30).
security_impact: low. Preempt tokens are single-use and short-lived. Access controls: only clients with stream:preempt scope can request preemption; added unit tests for scope enforcement.
related_work: Links: Linear ENG-9412 (priority scheduling), RFC #382 (stream resume semantics), previous PRs: pr-734215 (resumable session broker) and pr-421990 (deferred cancel session rehydration) — this PR focuses on reclaim/preemption rather than resumable handoff.
changelog_entry: Feature: server preemptive cancel + orphaned stream reclamation (opt-in via feature flag).
